correctness.rationale: At a stationary observation time S=r times the reset age is unit exponential, and the conditional centered Gaussian has variance (D/(πνΛ))h(S/x). The exponential Laplace transform gives the stated mean and frequency-pair covariance, hence the exact standardized fourth moment. For h(z)=sqrt(πz)erf(sqrt(z))+exp(-z)-1, its elasticity decreases strictly: the logarithmic derivative of the ratio A/B in the proof is the difference of the negative means of two tilted laws and is negative by their strictly increasing density ratio. Thus for x₂>x₁, h(S/x₂)/h(S/x₁) is strictly increasing in S. Weighting the exponential law by h(S/x₁)^2 instead of h(S/x₁) strictly increases the expectation of the squared ratio; Jensen then gives strict monotonicity. For the small-x endpoint the difference between h(z) and sqrt(πz)-1 lies in [0,exp(-z)] by the Gaussian tail bound; changing variables S=xz shows its contributions to both raw profile moments are O(x). For the large-x endpoint the exponential moments and the integral Taylor remainder give E[h]=1/x-1/(3x²)+O(x⁻³), E[h²]=2/x²-2/x³+O(x⁻⁴). Both expansions match, and dominated continuity gives the stated open range. Identification uses standardized excess kurtosis, not the unnormalized fourth moment without knowledge of D. The independent age-space quadrature /workspace/review_checks/check_3.py corroborates both asymptotic regimes; it is not the proof of monotonicity.
